## Summary

**Günther von Hohenstein is a saga invention** in Book VI: a young brother of the Teutonic Order (22 in 1353, about 30 in 1361), fluent in Lithuanian from a Curonian nurse of the Ragnit march, who asks to serve at Ragnit, is the third knight to take [Kęstutis](kestutis.qmd) at [Lake Ublik](../places/lake_ublik.qmd), carries and translates the prisoner's meals at Marienburg, and stands at Kaunas in 1362. He is the honest enemy of the Order's side. He is **not** the 1381 informant: that was [Kuno von Liebenstein](liebenstein.qmd).

## Appearance & tells

Fair-haired, with a childlike, puzzled face, "the face of people who have not yet worked out what faith costs" (Book VI ch. 14, age 22); about thirty when he takes Kęstutis (ch. 16), where the bewilderment is still on him; he speaks Lithuanian in an old, soft Curonian dialect, so gentle his voice sounds almost womanly (ch. 19). He wears the Order's white mantle, lowers his sword like a man who has not come to kill, gives his word, and asks to carry the prisoner's meals himself. Tells: he repeats a sentence a third time; he admires and cannot bear it.

## Want · Need · Lie · Truth

| | |
|---|---|
| **Want** (external) | To save lives by giving terms: to receive Kęstutis's surrender and stop the killing. |
| **Need** (internal) | To find out whether the crusade is a faith or a ledger. |
| **Lie** they believe | That the Order's cause and its terms are honest; that one honourable enemy can be reconciled to being an enemy. |
| **Truth** they learn (or refuse) | That Kęstutis cannot be bought or trusted by any word of his, since he will never say it unless he means it: “He did not swear. I begged.” (Book VI ch. 17). |

## Arc by book

- **Book VI (1353-1362):** at Kniprode's feast he sits uneasy among the Order's guests and says aloud that the heathen duke keeps every word (ch. 14, 1353); takes Kęstutis at Lake Ublik, offers terms and is refused (ch. 16, March 1361); asks to carry the prisoner's meals and translates between the duke and the Grand Master (ch. 17, Marienburg); lifts Vaidotas out of the ruins at Kaunas and gives his word that women and children in the inner tower will be spared (ch. 19, Easter 1362).

## Power & magic

Tier 0. No gift and no bargain: the saga uses him as proof that the Order is made of men and not only of the [Iron Saint](../forces/iron_saint.qmd)'s egregore. He is on the Order's side of the line, and his one act of mercy is to speak Lithuanian.

## Record vs saga

- **[Record]:** A real Günther von Hohenstein (c. 1310-1380) was komtur of Osterode from 1349 and later of Brandenburg; he is attested only weakly (a Russian archaeology press release) and in any case died before 1381, so he cannot have warned Kęstutis.
- **[Saga invention]:** The young brother, his Lithuanian, his terms offered at Ublik, the meals and translation at Marienburg (Book VI ch. 14, 16, 17, 19). The old canon line that he "warned Kęstutis in 1381" is withdrawn; the afterword of Book VI says so.

## Pronunciation

**GÜN-ter fon HO-en-štain** (/ˈɡʏntɐ fɔn ˈhoːənʃtaɪn/), English respelling *GUEN-ter fon HOH-en-shtine*; the saga's Lithuanian form is *Günteris fon Hohensteinas*. [world_rules/pronunciation_lexicon.json]

## Appearances

**Book VI:** ch. 14, 16, 17, 19 and the afterword. Not to be confused with [Kuno von Liebenstein](liebenstein.qmd), the real 1381 informant who appears in Book I ch. 1.
